## Purpose

Page through stored morning reports visible to the caller, newest first, with the
same per-report content `report_get` returns.

## When a playbook uses it

A step that needs recent reports without knowing their ids, such as finding
today's report or checking whether yesterday's finalized. `aq report list` reads
the same command.

## How it works internally

`src/commands/report_commands.py` validates the page (`offset` 0 or more, `limit`
1–100, default 50) and calls `list_morning_reports` in
`src/database/queries/morning_report_queries.py`, narrowed to the principal's
project when one is enforced. Each row passes the same visibility check and
project narrowing as `report_get`; rows the caller may not read are dropped from
the page.

## Side effects and persistence

None.

## Failure modes and diagnostics

`invalid_pagination` means `offset` was negative or `limit` fell outside 1–100. An
empty list means no stored report is visible in this scope; when the schedule is
enabled, `morning_report_tick`'s `next_due_at` says when the next one is due.

## Example step

```yaml
id: recent-morning
kind: command
command: report_list
args:
  limit: 7
```
